issue.title: streamlit chat_input callback (on_submit) not returning the message you input
issue.body: ### Checklist ### Summary The image below shows a test I'm running to show the issue. The error happens after running streamlit run app.py on the terminal and writing a message on the chat_input box that appears on screen. Once you press enter, this error happens. I think the error happens because the streamlit callback is not returning anything. If you use the second function (print_args) you will see that it's not printing anything in any of the variables that could be outputting something. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # Code to reproduce the first error: # You need to start the app with streamlit run app.py first import streamlit def print_text(chat_input): print(chat_input) streamlit.chat_input("Start a conversation!", on_submit=print_text) # Code to reproduce the second error: import streamlit def print_args(*args, **kwargs): print("Args:", args) print("Kwargs:", kwargs) streamlit.chat_input("Start a conversation!", on_submit=print_args) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce To reproduce both error you need to open a terminal, navigate to where the app.py file that contains the code above is located and execute: streamlit run app.py Then you have to open a browser window (if it doesn't open for you directly), write localhost:8501 and enter a message in the chat box that will appear on your browser ### Expected Behavior If this was working as I'm expecting it to work, the callback would return the message that the user passed as a variable like the on_change argument works in a streamlit.text_input block. ### Current Behavior TypeError: print_text() missing 1 required positional argument: 'chat_input' Traceback: File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py", line 548, in _run_script self._session_state.on_script_will_rerun(rerun_data.widget_states) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/safe_session_state.py", line 68, in on_script_will_rerun self._state.on_script_will_rerun(latest_widget_states) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 484, in on_script_will_rerun self._call_callbacks() File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 497, in _call_callbacks self._new_widget_state.call_callback(wid) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 249, in call_callback callback(*args, **kwargs) ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.24.0 - Python version: 3.11.3 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Google Chrome - Virtual environment: Docker container on a python slim buster base image ### Additional Information _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR? - [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

comments.body:
@micheldc55 This is the expected behavior. The `chat_input` value is not passed to the callback as a parameter, but instead, you can access it from the session state:

```python
import streamlit
def print_text():
    print(st.session_state.user_input)

streamlit.chat_input("Start a conversation!", on_submit=print_text, key="user_input")
```

It could also be a nice feature to access via a function parameter. Feel free to create a feature request for this.
